title: MEPC.328(76) entry into force corrected from 1 January 2023 to 1 November 2022, with the application date kept as its own limb
rationale: H5's source-corpus consistency pass (brief section 30) compared every MIW card citing MEPC.328(76) and found the product contradicting itself. QB3_C, QB6 and QB7_C state the revised MARPOL Annex VI is in force 1 November 2022. QB7_A#q1 and QB7_A_CheatSheet.html stated 1 January 2023, in six places between them, three of which called it the 'entry into force' outright. Two pages of one product giving different entry-into-force dates for one resolution is a candidate-facing contradiction, and a candidate revising from QB7_A would have quoted the wrong one to a panel that asks this verbatim. Verified at primary source: MEPC.328(76) operative paragraph 2 determines deemed acceptance on 1 May 2022 and operative paragraph 3 states the amendments 'shall enter into force on 1 November 2022', read from the held PDF (SHA-256 1EE317601C6C44EBFDD4144A6E8CCE59CD2455C939EE40FB1390103A8C50BF08) recorded in the shared true-source corpus at 7441cc0. The resolution was adopted 17 June 2021. 1 January 2023 is not a fabricated date and is not deleted: it is the date the CII and SEEMP Part III OBLIGATIONS begin to apply, the first data-collection year. The defect was collapsing two limbs into one, which is the same shape as CORR-LSA-LIFEBOAT-VENTILATION-20260822, where a two-limb application rule was reduced to its new-build limb and thereby inverted for the existing fleet. All six statements now carry both dates as two distinct facts.
note: Known trap 59 already recorded this exact proposition - it was registered during the H series - and it did not catch these six statements, because its GREP named one spelling of the wrong value, '1 November 2023'. QB7_A carried a different wrong rendering of the same fact. The shared corpus independently hit a third, 'EIF 2023-01-01', in its own amendment register. Entry 59 is extended here with the second variant, with the two-limb statement, and with the general rule: a banned-phrase guard protects against the spelling you saw, not the fact you got wrong, so where a date is the subject the guard must assert the PROPOSITION and fail on any other value. That is what validate_correction_annexvi_eif.py does - it does not list wrong dates, it requires the right one and rejects any entry-into-force claim for this resolution that gives another. It earned that shape immediately: its closed-world pass found an eighth occurrence in QB7_C spelled 'MEPC 76', which no search for 'MEPC.328(76)' could have found. The rest of QB7_A#q1 was rechecked while open: the 5,000 GT threshold, Regulation 26 as the SEEMP basis, Regulation 28 as the CII rating framework, MEPC.346(78) as the SEEMP development guidelines, MEPC.347(78) as the flag-State verification guidelines, the 3-consecutive-years-at-D and 1-year-at-E corrective-action triggers, and the EU ETS (1 January 2024 for shipping) and FuelEU Maritime (Regulation 2023/1805, 1 January 2025) dates all verified correct and are unchanged.
content_index_effect: None. Question text, anchors and card positions are unchanged; only answer-body and reference-table wording moved. build_qb_content_index --check is a no-op across this correction.

artefacts.rationale: Carries no q-card, so it takes no digest pin, but it held two of the six wrong statements - one in the SEEMP Part III card body and one in the Master Numbers reference table - and a candidate memorises a cheat sheet before reading the card behind it. Leaving it stale would have reproduced exactly the failure CORR-DEFN-TREATY-20260825 found, where a correction fixed the card and left four candidate-facing copies of the wrong model on the sheet beside it. Both statements now carry the entry-into-force date and the application date as two things.

cards.rationale: Four surfaces of this one card carried the defect and were corrected together: the answer body's SEEMP Part III paragraph, the Key Numbers list, the reference table's MEPC.328(76) row, and the Deep Dive numbers list. Each now states 1 November 2022 as the entry into force of the amendments and 1 January 2023 as the first year the obligations apply. Question text, anchor and card position are unchanged.

An EIGHTH occurrence, and it was found by this correction's own content gate rather than by the sweep that opened the correction. QB7_C's 'Numbers to Memorise' line read 'MEPC 76 - June 2021, in force 1 Jan 2023'. Every targeted search for this defect had looked for 'MEPC.328(76)'; this page spells the resolution 'MEPC 76', so no such search could ever have found it - which is precisely why the gate asserts the PROPOSITION over every citing page instead of grepping for a wrong string. The page in fact carried FOUR statements of the fact, and the gate found the other three only once a control byte was removed from its own regex -- a literal 0x08 where a word boundary belonged, which is trap 1 of SKILL section 6 and made the pattern silently unmatchable. Three were wrong (the 15-second answer, the Key Dates block and the Numbers to Memorise line) and one was already right (the regulatory-reference row). The three now name the resolution in full, gives adoption June 2021, entry into force 1 Nov 2022, and application from 1 Jan 2023. Elsewhere on the same page the card already stated 'in force 1 Nov 2022' correctly, so this page had been contradicting itself internally as well.
